gaps.sentence: If the appeals court ___ the verdict, the case will be reheard in the autumn.
gaps.explanation: Present simple after 'if', will + infinitive in the main clause.

gaps.sentence: I wish I ___ taller, but genes are genes.
gaps.hint: an impossible present wish with were
gaps.explanation: For impossible present wishes, formal English uses 'were': were.

gaps.sentence: If the temperature ___ below freezing tonight, the race will be postponed.
gaps.explanation: First conditional: present simple in the if-clause, will + infinitive in the result.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ more at university!
gaps.explanation: 'If only + past perfect' — regret about a past failure.

gaps.sentence: If only I ___ faster — we might still catch the train.
gaps.hint: if only plus could, present inability
gaps.explanation: 'If only' plus 'could' expresses a present inability you regret: could run.

gaps.sentence: If the red light ___, the machine needs servicing.
gaps.hint: a general rule stated with if
gaps.explanation: Rules and general facts use the present simple in the if-clause: flashes.

gaps.sentence: ___ there be any problems, call this number.
What will you do if the train ___ before you get there?
gaps.explanation: Even in questions about the future, the if-clause uses the present simple: leaves.
